subject: CLOSE statement
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB235). GR7's two halves, both settled and the observable one now PINNED rather than accidental. HALF (a) - if file-name-1 is in a SAME RECORD AREA clause and any OTHER file connector named in that clause is open, the area stays AVAILABLE after the CLOSE - is the half a program can observe, and it holds STRUCTURALLY: DataBinder.BindIoControl binds Format 2 by pointing every member's first record at one shared anchor (12.4.6.4.4 GR2, cite.py OK), so the area is a live typed field of the emitted program class for the whole runtime element and no CLOSE path can take it from a still-open sibling. pb235_same_record_area_close is the spec-derived golden that measures it end to end: two files in ONE SAME RECORD AREA clause, a READ of FA filling the shared area, a CLOSE FA while FB is open leaving the record readable through both record-names, a READ of FB then making the area FB's record (12.4.6.4.4 GR2's 'most recently-read file open in the input mode'), and a CLOSE FA UNIT proving the UNIT phrase changes nothing - GR7 governs 'the CLOSE statement WITHOUT the UNIT phrase'. The clause's binding site now CITES GR7, so the rule is written down where the area is created. HALF (b) - with no member open, a successful CLOSE makes the area UNAVAILABLE - carries NO OBSERVABLE OBLIGATION: the standard defines no behaviour for referencing an unavailable record area, and Annex A.2 item 5 makes the unsuccessful-CLOSE case outright undefined ('The unsuccessful execution of the CLOSE statement without the UNIT phrase leaves the availability of the record area undefined'). It is therefore a DETERMINATION, not an implementation gap, and it is stated at docs/CONFORMANCE.md 7 (A.1 item 24): the storage keeps its last content for the life of the runtime element - the answer every surveyed implementation gives - and the golden's final line pins it, labelled in the source as the determination rather than as the standard's answer so it cannot be misread as a conformance claim. The previous PARTIAL's charge that 'the implementation cannot tell case (a) from case (b)' is answered by that determination: under it the two cases have the same realization, so there is nothing to tell apart.
